subject: mt-info
title: MT.INFO.------ TRS.
description: Diagram in CMOA(I)-13 (Creative Music Outside of America, Level One — Britain/Germany/Holland), first of two on book p219. Accompanies Braxton's structural turn: 'it becomes more a question of musicians celebrating their creativity in accordance with the vibrational dictates of their environment as well as their own cultural and vibrational pull.' MT-INFO (multi-information) is crossed with TRS (transference): the question is what multi-information produces when crossed with transference — under conditions where each European musician is celebrating both environment and personal vibration. C-INFO (composite information) and PHY-U-FUND (physical universe fundamental) form the upper-center cluster. LANG-DY (language dynamics) feeds in from the upper-left. TRS itself is the partner. TR-INFO (transfer information) sits between subject and partner on the left. PART (participation) sits below the subject. P-PROG (positive progression) anchors the right output. CULT-SOLD (culture solidification) hangs on the lower-right. PRI-INFO (principle information) anchors the bottom-center. Structural argument: multi-information crossed with transference is fed by composite-information and physical-universe-fundamental from above and by language-dynamics from below-left. The lower output cluster (participation, principle-information, culture-solidification, positive-progression) registers the productive structure of European creativity: when multi-information genuinely crosses with transference, the productive output is *participation rooted in principle-information* that produces culture-solidification and positive-progression. The diagram is Braxton's structural case for why European creativity has a chance to make a real contribution — the upstream tests (composite-information, physical-universe-fundamental, language-dynamics) ground the crossing in actual conditions.
